calls.title: Kenneth & James
calls.summary: The team is gearing up to launch the major brand Object, migrating from Contentful to Sanity, which marks a significant move in migrating brands from legacy systems. Kenneth highlighted the ongoing influx of tasks as the team prepares for launch, adopting a pragmatic 'go live and see what happens' approach. The launch schedule is influenced by peak season timing, with brands avoiding go-lives during busy periods. The rollout strategy initially targets about 10 bestseller brands with a dual fee model while allowing for future expansion through renegotiation. They aim to start setup and testing in summer 2023, with close vendor support prioritized in the initial phases. To secure internal buy-in, a strong ROI case is being developed based on analytics to measure performance improvements, with an emphasis on collaboration and in-person meetings to finalize agreements.
calls.keywords: product launch, brand onboarding, commercial structure, testing platform, peak season, partnership negotiation

calls.title: Kenneth & James Check in
calls.summary:
# Kenneth & James Check in
Date: 2026-10-07 | Duration: 20m

## Summary
The team agreed to begin with a Pro subscription proof of concept rather than immediately adopting Enterprise, because Enterprise pricing, implementation risk, and uncertain adoption require clear ROI first. Kenneth emphasized minimizing risk, building internal buy-in incrementally, and scaling only after success signals emerge. Enterprise could become more feasible once ROI is demonstrated and dedicated internal resources, potentially including a full-time hire, are available. Development of the new UI component has not started, as previous work was paused and current priorities include open source testing and two brand launches this year. Resource constraints and timing are the main blockers, while one brand has identified the new solution as a high priority. James proposed a no-cost, time-boxed POC with Enterprise access, solutions-engineer support, and a Slack channel for integration assistance. Kenneth requested written details for internal comparison. Both agreed to pause until capacity improves, after which they will revisit timing and progress. (02:04–08:16)

## Keywords
Product subscription, proof of concept, ROI evaluation, resource allocation, brand launch, enterprise support

## Action Items

**James Shannon**
Formalize and send a written proposal for a no-cost, no-contract Enterprise proof of concept (POC) including dedicated support resources and clearly defined time-box parameters (07:35)
Follow up with Kenneth on timing and readiness to initiate the POC after internal considerations and resource availability (08:17)

**Kenneth Christiansen**
Review James’s written POC proposal and compare it against proceeding independently with the Pro subscription (07:53)
Decide on timing and allocate resources to prioritize starting the POC implementation after current brand launches are completed (04:01)
